answer: Sybil resistance comes from requiring each identity to complete a long, ordered chain of modular squarings, with each result depending on the previous one. GPUs can run separate chains, but cannot parallelize the dependency sequence for a clone, so creating many valid identities imposes a real elapsed-time bottleneck. A Wesolowski proof lets peers verify the delay efficiently; onyx, nadir, and velvet offer no shortcut around the sequential work.
